items.title: Which animal records contain Burmese text-quality issues?
assumptions: Visible typo findings are limited to high-confidence spelling and repetition patterns; ambiguous zoological common names are not classified as errors.
Legacy Unicode spelling forms are reported separately from obvious visible typos.

source.label: Wildlife animal database
filters: 28 published Burmese or Burmese-facing text fields
Internal provenance JSON, URLs, and image fields excluded
caveats: Automated and manual pattern review can identify high-confidence issues but cannot prove that every free-text Burmese sentence is linguistically perfect.
The scan did not modify any animal record.

evidenceFlow.title: Read-only animal records
evidenceFlow.detail: Published Burmese-facing fields were read from the local animals table through SQLite read-only mode.

evidenceFlow.title: Text-quality checks
evidenceFlow.detail: The review checked repeated code points, repeated words or phrases, curated high-confidence spelling patterns, legacy Unicode spelling forms, and repeated normalized Burmese animal names.

sourceRoles.label: wildlife.db
sourceRoles.role: Animal names and published Burmese text fields used in the audit.

source.label: Wildlife animal database
filters: Duplicate after trimming name_my, normalizing Unicode, and removing zero-width joiner characters
Different scientific species retained for manual review
caveats: A shared vernacular name is not necessarily a spelling error.

evidenceFlow.title: Duplicate-name grouping
evidenceFlow.detail: Trimmed, Unicode-normalized Burmese names with zero-width joiner characters removed were grouped, and groups with more than one animal record were returned.

sourceRoles.label: wildlife.db
sourceRoles.role: Burmese, English, and scientific animal names used to identify shared common names.
